name: What's the difference between patching and re-plastering walls?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between patching and re-plastering walls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Patching refers to repairing a localized area of damage, like a hole or crack, using materials such as drywall compound or spackle. It's suitable for minor imperfections to restore a smooth surface. Re-plastering, on the other hand, involves applying a new layer of plaster or a skim coat over an entire wall or a substantial section. This is done to achieve a uniform finish, smooth out extensive texture, or cover widespread surface damage, effectively creating a new wall surface.
acceptedAnswer.description: Patching fixes small, localized damage. Re-plastering applies a new layer over a large area for a uniform finish or to cover widespread damage.
